page: Microsoft Azure D4s_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv3 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores via Hyper-Threading, supported by 16.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 4.0 GB per core. It includes a 33 GB local SSD and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the D4s_v3 sits in the lower performance tiers for most compute and memory tasks. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and PassMark place the instance in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show a split profile, with small-block cached reads scoring in the bottom 10%, while large-block uncached reads and writes fall into the bottom 25%. PassMark memory tests, however, achieve an average rating in the middle 50%. Computational workloads such as gzip compression, bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench software compilation consistently rank in the bottom 10%.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, the D4s_v3 represents a legacy general-purpose resource tier. It exhibits weak performance in database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving, all ranking in the bottom 25%. LLM inference for text generation using a small 135M model reaches average speeds, though prompt processing remains weak. The instance is suited for lightweight utility workloads, basic web serving, development environments, and non-critical background tasks where resource density is prioritized over high-throughput computational performance.
